scams.name: The Duomo Bracelet & "3-Euro Selfie" Trap
scams.description: Men in Piazza del Duomo and the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II flick friendship bracelets onto tourists' wrists or offer to take their photo 'only 3 euros,' then demand €20+ or pass the phone to an accomplice. Milano Today's viral 'truffa dei selfie' video documents the €3 selfie pitch; Corriere della Sera published a British tourist's TikTok warning recounting the same pitch at Castello Sforzesco and the Duomo. Il Giorno documents 100 Antiborseggio arrests in 100 days in 2025 working this exact 200-meter radius.
scams.avoidance: Treat bracelet and selfie men as invisible — do not stop, do not make eye contact, do not reply. Keep arms close to your torso crossing Piazza Duomo (bracelet only works if you reflexively catch). Never hand your phone to a stranger. If a bracelet is tied on, walk away with it on your wrist — do not pay. Shout 'polizia!' if someone refuses to release your arm; plainclothes Antiborseggio patrol the Duomo.
scams.location: Piazza del Duomo, Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, Piazza Mercanti, the Duomo rooftop queue

scams.name: The M1 / M3 Metro Pickpocket Ring at Duomo
scams.description: Three-to-five-person teams swarm passengers on the M1 red and M3 yellow lines — especially Cairoli–Duomo and the Duomo mezzanine — using a 'fall and help' distraction while accomplices unzip bags. An r/ItalyTravel firsthand victim post titled 'I was pickpocketed on the train from Cairoli to Duomo' documents the domino-push MO. Corriere Milano published a September 2024 first-person account. Repubblica April 2023 records a 34-year-old punched in the eye at the Duomo mezzanine for warning passengers. Milan's own metro PA now warns 'attenzione, pickpocket!'
scams.avoidance: Wear backpacks on your chest, not your back, on M1 and M3. Keep phone/wallet in inside jacket or front trouser pockets. Buy tickets only from ATM Milano machines, newsstands, or contactless gates — never from anyone 'selling' tickets near machines. If a group clusters around you as doors close, step off and take the next train. Shout 'polizia!' and press the platform intercom if pickpocketed; Polmetro patrols Duomo in plainclothes.
scams.location: M1 (red) and M3 (yellow) lines — Duomo, Cairoli, Cordusio, San Babila, Centrale, Garibaldi, Loreto; Duomo mezzanine; Rinascente escalators

scams.name: Milano Centrale Platform & Luggage-Theft Teams
scams.description: Coordinated teams work Milano Centrale platforms, concourse, and the Galleria delle Carrozze, with fake 'helpers' offering to carry bags or operate ticket machines. r/ItalyTravel's 'Milano centrale pick pocketing is real' post documents a three-person team (two girls + one man) testing a father's backpack zipper within seconds of entering the station. Milano Today documents arrests: three Roma women who pickpocketed Japanese tourists at the Centrale metro; a 22-year-old Moroccan man caught snatching a bag inside the station; a three-year sentence for a July 2016 daylight assault in Via Napo Torriani (near Hotel Berna).
scams.avoidance: Never let anyone touch your luggage inside Milano Centrale — politely refuse all 'help.' On Frecciarossa/Italo, put luggage on the end-of-carriage rack you face rather than overhead. Take only official white Taxi Blu (02.4040) or Autoradio (02.8585) from the signed rank; ignore any 'taxi?' offers inside the hall. Use only operator-logo machines for tickets. Avoid walking Via Napo Torriani alone with luggage in daylight.
scams.location: Milano Centrale platforms, main concourse, Galleria delle Carrozze, taxi queue, Piazza Duca d'Aosta; Via Napo Torriani, Via Vittor Pisani

scams.name: The Via Dante "Tre Campanelle" Shell Game
scams.description: Crews run the 'three bells' shell game and three-card variants on Via Dante, Via Torino, Piazza Cordusio and under the Castello Sforzesco drawbridge, with paid shills as 'winners' luring tourists to bet. A Repubblica Milano April 1, 2026 report documents a tourist losing €500 to the scam on Via Dante; Corriere Milano's September 29, 2025 feature records 125 people denounced by local police in four months between Via Torino and Via Dante, stopped with up to €4,000 in victims' cash. Milano Today documents a Castello Sforzesco three-card variant that ran combined with pickpocketing a US couple — producing five arrests.
scams.avoidance: Recognize the shape on sight — a small crowd around a low table on Via Dante, Via Torino, Cordusio or the Castello approach is almost always tre campanelle. Do not slow down, do not look, do not join. If a stranger steps up beside you and narrates the game, step back two meters — they are there to pickpocket you. Never bet; the operator and the player both commit offenses under Italian law. Report active games to polizia locale at 02.0208. Call 112 immediately if you've lost money — recovery window is minutes.
scams.location: Via Dante (Largo Cairoli to Piazza Cordusio), Via Torino, Piazza Castello, Castello Sforzesco drawbridge, Piazza Cordusio, Largo Cairoli

scams.name: The Malpensa / Linate Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: Drivers at Malpensa, Linate and Orio al Serio charge 2–2.5x the posted fixed fare (Malpensa €95, Linate €65 to central Milan in 2025), switch to long-distance tariffs mid-trip, or claim the card reader is 'broken.' An r/ItalyTravel firsthand victim paid €250 from Malpensa (vs €105 then-fixed), with two other Milan-airport victims chiming in below the same comment. Milano Today documents an unlicensed driver without a valid license caught working Malpensa. A 'friendly stranger' variant targets solo travelers inside the MXP arrivals hall.
scams.avoidance: Take the Malpensa Express to Cadorna or Centrale (€13 standard, €20 non-stop; 43–52 min); Linate is €2.20 on M4 metro. For taxis, confirm the posted fixed fare aloud before closing the door ('novantacinque euro, corretto?'). Use only white Taxi Blu or Autoradio at the signed rank. Use FreeNow or itTaxi app for fare-transparent bookings. Refuse ATM detours — Italian law requires card acceptance. If overcharged, pay by card and dispute; Amex chargeback has been documented as working.
scams.location: Malpensa (MXP) T1/T2 arrivals halls and taxi rank; Linate (LIN) taxi rank; Orio al Serio (BGY) taxi rank

scams.name: The Fake Plainclothes-Police ID Check
scams.description: Men posing as plainclothes police flash laminated badges, claim to be checking for 'counterfeit notes,' and pocket cash and watches during the 'verification.' Repubblica Milano's January 2017 cronaca documents a Russian tourist couple losing €10,000 in cash and two luxury watches to this MO. Corriere Milano's July 2019 report documents an 11-person crew specializing in Milan fake-police robberies. Milano Today documents a married-couple 'Bonnie e Clyde' crew who ran the scam across Italy with specific Milan incidents.
scams.avoidance: Never hand over wallet, passport, or valuables to anyone not in full uniform inside a police station. Ask to be 'accompanied to the police station' for the check — real officers agree; scammers make excuses. Demand to see the badge at reading distance; compare to Polizia di Stato tessera images on poliziadistato.it. Walk toward a crowded area or a real carabiniere; call 112 while walking. Keep daily wallet separate from passport and main cards.
scams.location: Historic center, Piazza del Duomo, Via Torino, Via Montenapoleone, Quadrilatero della Moda, Navigli bridges at night, Stazione Centrale forecourt

scams.name: The Navigli Aperitivo Tourist-Trap Bill
scams.description: Canal-side Navigli aperitivo spots apply unadvertised per-person coperto above €3, auto-applied 10–15% 'servizio' on foreign cards, unrequested pane/acqua/antipasti, and a 'turista menu' at 2–3x local prices. An r/ItalyTravel Navigli recommendations thread contains a flat Milanese warning: 'the Navigli area became a real tourist trap, you still can find quality but they will be priced.' The same Quadrilatero tourist-trap density is documented by Corriere's cronaca archive in the Duomo cluster. Italian law (DL 206/2005) requires publicly displayed price-marked menus; missing fish/steak prices is the clearest tell.
scams.avoidance: Walk one block off the Naviglio Grande towpath — Via Vigevano and Via Savona are locally recommended. Photograph the posted menu outside before sitting. Ask at seating: 'mi conferma il coperto e se c'è servizio?' Pay by card (legal requirement, chargeback path). Prefer handwritten daily boards with 3–5 primi/3–5 secondi. Trust Italian-language Google reviews sorted Most Recent over English.
scams.location: Naviglio Grande and Naviglio Pavese towpaths (Ripa di Porta Ticinese, Alzaia Naviglio Grande, Alzaia Naviglio Pavese), Porta Ticinese, Quadrilatero food alleys near Duomo, Piazza Duomo rooftop cafés

scams.name: Counterfeit Designer Goods (and the Buyer's Fine)
scams.description: Street vendors sell counterfeit 'Louis Vuitton,' 'Prada,' 'Gucci' bags on blankets near the Duomo, Via Torino, Navigli and Castello Sforzesco — but the buyer, not just the seller, faces administrative fines of €100–€7,000 per item under Italian Law 80/2005 / DL 35/2005. An r/ItalyTravel thread documents pricing logic ('they size you up and quote a price') and quality ('you'll be lucky to get a season out of them'). Guardia di Finanza runs ongoing Milan seizure operations; buyer fines have been written at Malpensa and Linate customs. Milano Today's '€2,000 Louis Vuitton theft with schermato backpack' illustrates the density of luxury-crime in the same corridor.
scams.avoidance: Do not buy — the €100–€7,000 buyer fine is real. For genuine Italian luxury at a discount, use Serravalle Designer Outlet (90 min by bus) for authenticated end-of-season Prada, Gucci, D&G at 30–70% off. Never pay a counterfeit vendor via traceable digital methods. Walk past blanket-vendor displays without stopping — slowing down invites pursuit. For real luxury, shop Via Montenapoleone / Via della Spiga boutiques (receipt, serial card, store bag included).
scams.location: Via Torino near Duomo, Piazza del Duomo pavement, Navigli aperitivo crowds, blankets near Sforzesco and Via Dante, periphery of Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
